mechanism_narrative: Low levels of the federal funds rate, indicative of an accommodative monetary policy stance, predict positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC between FEDFUNDS level and 20-day SPX returns remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or 20-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) in the entire sample.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a tightening monetary policy that depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or the Rank IC over 2-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate and the consumer price index signal a tightening monetary policy amid rising inflation, which compresses equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction effect fails if the Rank IC between the joint signal (FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both rising) and 20-day SPX returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or if the negative return signal is not significant (p>0.05) in the interaction group.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, a decline in the unemployment rate below 4.0% signals labor market tightness that accelerates inflation and prompts monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances during late-cycle expansions when UNRATE < 4.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment indicates robust labor market conditions that support corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC between PAYEMS level and 20-day SPX returns remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or 20-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) in the entire sample.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts fall below 1,200,000 units, it signals a weakening in the housing sector and broader economic demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST < 1200.0, or the Rank IC over 2-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and industrial production signal a broad-based economic slowdown, which triggers risk-off sentiment and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction effect fails if the Rank IC between the joint signal (HOUST and INDPRO both declining) and 20-day SPX returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or if the negative return signal is not significant (p>0.05) in the interaction group.

mechanism_narrative: In early-cycle recoveries, a sustained increase in industrial production above 110.0 (index 2017=100) signals strengthening economic activity that boosts corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances during early-cycle recoveries when INDPRO > 110.0, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
